name: PCB Timelapse
description: Record your PCB layout as a timelapse: the zoomed editor view plus a clean whole-board view, rendered to video.
description_full:
AI-written: the code was written almost entirely by Claude under the author's direction, and tested on Windows with KiCad 10.

PCB Timelapse records two streams while you lay out a board: what you see in the editor (zoom, active layer) and the whole board, re-drawn cleanly from snapshots with no ratsnest or cursor.

Recording only runs while the PCB Editor is in front; alt-tab, sleep and the lock screen pause it. Board snapshots come from your saves and KiCad's autosave, so the plugin never touches the live board.

Render from a dialog inside KiCad: pick layers and their order, KiCad-style holes and vias, board fill, combined side-by-side or stacked video, and join several recordings into one. The board video follows the copper layer you were working on.

Rendering needs a separate Python 3 with pymupdf and pillow, and ffmpeg on PATH. Recording needs nothing extra.
